Variants.Content: The Fortress is located on the northern coast of the Westerlands and is the seat of House Bamfort. Facing the direction of the Sunset Sea and the Iron Islands, this place has long lived in the memory of pirates, raids and bad weather; "disaster" is not a prophecy, but a sober naming of risks by seaside people. High walls, signal fires, small boats that can be launched into the water, and fishermen who are familiar with the reefs all form a defense. Heavy armored knights alone cannot hold the long coast. The Fortress is connected to Lannisport, Fairy City, and inland roads, but it maintains the tense pace of a coastal stronghold.

Entry Banefort Local families also relied on mining tunnels, pastures, mountain roads, gold and silver circulation and the market sheltered by Casterly Rock; if any road, well or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Banefort They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the West; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hooves.

Entry Banefort If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Stone and wood will decay, but the fortress still relies on craftsmen to take care of shipbuilding wood, canvas, salt, fish catch, and stones to resist the sea breeze. It relies on priests to preserve the stone carvings left by the Seven Gods, family tombs, and the authority of the lord. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Banefort They care about the mines, pastures, mountain roads, the circulation of gold and silver, and the market under the protection of Casterly Rock. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see the coat of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
